just >= 1.36 makes duplicate variable definitions a hard parse error, which broke the documented override pattern: a downstream justfile redefining a staged variable (python_cmd and friends) after the import? line failed with 'variable X has multiple definitions' the moment .just/ was staged (observed on wowsp: just dev refused to start). common.just now carries exactly one set directive - allow-duplicate-variables - as a documented exception to its set-free composition rule: under it the ROOT definition wins, which is precisely the downstream-customization semantics the header has always advertised. just < 1.36 tolerated duplicates silently. Staged-file version 0.7.0 -> 0.7.1.
